out.other_title: Debates can converge confidently on an incorrect answer
out.rationale: Du et al. report debates can converge confidently on an incorrect answer. Choi, Zhu and Li prove that under their condition (1) an agent's belief sequence is a martingale: its expected belief at the next round equals its current belief. They state that this neutral expectation means that, without additional bias towards correct signals, debate alone does not guarantee convergence to the truth.
out.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether a martingale result for agents' beliefs in multi-agent debate bears on debates converging on incorrect answers

out.other_title: Debate can reach a correct answer when all agents start wrong
out.rationale: Du et al. conclude from qualitative cases where all agents start wrong but end right that debate does not only amplify an initially present correct answer. Choi, Zhu and Li prove that under their condition (1) an agent's belief sequence is a martingale: its expected belief at the next round equals its current belief; individual cases can still go wrong-to-right under a martingale.
out.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether multi-agent debate does more than amplify initial answers, studied through expected beliefs under condition (1) by Choi, Zhu and Li and through qualitative debate examples by Du et al.
